queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.
queries.steady: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.
queries.act: Turn toward what lasts: serve, study, reflect daily, and offer your work to something beyond yourself.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

prasang.title: 'I am drifting': a letter from Alameda (1900)
prasang.summary: Two years before his death, worn out, he writes that he has laid down the role of leader. He is glad he was born, glad he suffered, glad he made big blunders. He admits that ambition, personality, fear and love of power lay behind his work, and says they are fading as he drifts toward peace.
prasang.lesson: Honest looking back, with gratitude for the mistakes, can bring peace.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
alternates.sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
alternates.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
alternates.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
alternates.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.for_you: You have reached a place where looking back brings only peace, not regret. This gratitude for the whole path is a rare and quiet gift. Let it be the ground you stand on today.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha sums up the four gatekeepers of freedom.
verse.sanskrit: संतोषः परमो लाभः सत्सङ्गः परमा गतिः । विचारः परमं ज्ञानं शमो हि परमं सुखम् ॥
verse.line: Contentment is the greatest gain, good company the best path, clear thinking the best knowledge, calm the greatest joy.
verse.translation: Contentment is the greatest gain, good company the best path, inquiry the highest knowledge, and calm the greatest happiness.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.try_today: Notice the calm that sits beside your gratitude today.
verse.scene_line: You sit in your retirement, looking back, and find the path has led you well.

why: The four gatekeepers (Yoga Vasishtha, Mumukshu Prakarana 11-16)

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on the cycle of offering that sustains the world.
verse.sanskrit: देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः । परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
verse.line: Nourish one another, and together you'll reach the highest good.
verse.translation: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will attain the highest good.
verse.why: Life works by give and take; taking only for yourself breaks the cycle.

prasang.summary: Krishna describes action as offering, the mutual nourishing of humans and gods, and the wrong of taking without giving back.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः । लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
verse.line: Janaka and others reached fulfilment through action. Keep working, if only for the good of the world.
verse.translation: Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. And looking to the welfare of the world, you too should act.
verse.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.for_you: Your gratitude is a quiet strength. You have lived enough to see how action shaped your life. Let this feeling guide what you do next.
verse.try_today: Notice one small way your presence today can hold the world together.
verse.scene_line: You sit with your gratitude, like Janaka, and see how your life has unfolded.

why: acting for the holding together of the world

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.line: Work as hard as the ambitious do, but for everyone's good, not your own grip on results.
verse.translation: As the unwise act with attachment to their work, Bharata, so should the wise act without attachment, wishing to hold the world together.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.for_you: You want to hold on to this grateful feeling. You can keep it by loosening your grip on how it must last. The world stays together when you act without attachment to the outcome.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you release the need to hold on, and let the moment simply be.
verse.scene_line: You stand beside the wise one, acting with care but without the grip on the result.

why: Work for the good of all.
acting to hold the world together
plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is building something. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

guard.line: Senses in hand, even-minded everywhere, glad in the good of all beings: they reach me too.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verse.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verse.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

why: Courage and steadiness are the wheels of the chariot that wins; do not let fear decide.
Composure for those who depend on one

story.title: Bharata's fourteen-year wait ends
story.story_hook: For fourteen years Bharata had counted the days; now a stranger was telling him to stop.
story.summary: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.
story.lesson: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
story.hook_title: Bharata had counted the days for fourteen years, and then Hanuman arrived
story.teaser: Bharata had counted the days for fourteen years, and then Hanuman arrived
story.for_you: You have grown what was given to you, and now you can let it go with no claim left. That completion is enough. This is the quiet meaning of your years.

why: What is held in trust is to be grown and returned without claim; that completes a life's purpose.
